newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Edgy platinum shows upside scope.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Edgy platinum shows upside scope.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 21--------------
Platinum remains at centre stage
on Monday amid concerns about tightness in a jittery market, with $385 an ounce a realistic upside target, dealers said.
Gold and silver were seen range trading in the near term.
But gold remained vulnerable to the downside.
PLATINUM - Prices have the potential to jump by $5, $10 or even more in the near term as the market ponders the possibility of further delays to Russian supplies, dealers said.
"Platinum could easily move $10 higher or more while these concerns are around," a dealer said.

Platinum prices had shot up last week from a low of $354 amid rumours that a swap of 30 tonnes of Russian gold held by Union Bank of Switzerland as collateral against a hard currency loan for platinum and palladium might fall through.
Russian officials have denied any talks have taken place.
At 0755 GMT spot platinum was indicated at $380.50/$381.50, up from Friday's London close of $377.50/$378.50.
GOLD - Prices were barely budging in early trading from Friday's closing levels and dealers said they were not expecting gold to move immediately from a $340-$345 price band.
"Hopefully gold is just consolidating. But I could see it sharply lower," a dealer said.
"There may be attempts to try to push it down to the recent low of $336 and increases in open interest on Comex point to big short positions again."
At 0755 GMT spot gold was indicated at $342.60/$343.00, compared to Friday's London close of $342.20/$342.70.
SILVER - Prices were hovering at the 10-day moving average of $4.75, which might provide slight resistance, dealers said.
But silver's downside would be limited in the near term as the market was still on the oversold side, with the 14-day RSI at 36.5 percent.
At 0755 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.75/$4.77, unchanged from Friday's London close.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
